  • It has been revealed that coinbase is bringing crypto trading directly into ChatGPT as competition for AI-powered financial services intensifies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

Recent findings suggest that the CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

It has been revealed that coinbase is bringing crypto trading directly into ChatGPT as competition for AI-powered financial services intensifies. Meanwhile, PancakeSwap has dropped “Swap” from its name, expanding beyond decentralized trading. The two developments show how Coinbase and Binance-linked crypto projects are positioning themselves for the next phase of digital finance.

Coinbase confirmed its ChatGPT integration yesterday, allowing customers to connect accounts and manage portfolios. Users can check balances, analyze holdings, and place eligible trades using everyday language. And every order requires explicit approval before execution.

The timing coincides with Pancake’s attempt to reposition itself beyond its original decentralized exchange business.

Trade Base assets from ChatGPT@ChatGPT now connects to your Coinbase account, so you can trade Base assets in chat pic.twitter.com/tg9r2Iv3Qe.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

The Coinbase plugin allows eligible people to trade crypto and equities without leaving ChatGPT. Users can request market or limit orders through conversational instructions.

Sources indicate that before execution, ChatGPT displays an interactive confirmation card showing order details. Customers must approve the transaction before Coinbase processes it through its Advanced Trade platform. Standard trading fees, eligibility requirements, and account limits still apply.

Sources indicate that coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong described the integration as another step toward an emerging agentic economy. The idea involves AI assistants handling increasingly complex financial tasks for consumers. But Coinbase still keeps humans responsible for approving individual trades for now.

To decentralize AI and preserve freedom, we need a coordination layer: a market economy where agents communicate and cooperate through prices.Teams of specialized open-weight models can outperform frontier models, just as a team of skilled people can outperform any single….

In a recent development, the integration also builds on Coinbase’s AI infrastructure. Its Coinbase for Agents toolkit provides developers with connections to trading accounts and market data. The ChatGPT launch brings those capabilities into a more accessible consumer interface.

It has been revealed that as of today, the official integration at the moment remains limited to eligible U.S. Coinbase users. It also depends on ChatGPT account and workspace availability.

It has been revealed that fresh brand, who dis?PancakeSwap is now Pancake 🥞6 years ago we were known for one thing. Today, we’re More Than a Swap. Let us reintroduce ourselves 👇 pic.twitter.com/J3P7Mocu2P.

In a recent development, while Coinbase expands through ChatGPT, Pancake is changing how users perceive its decentralized trading ecosystem. Formerly known as PancakeSwap, the platform announced its rebrand today. The latest identity reflects six years of expansion beyond its original token-swapping business.

Pancake now operates across more than 11 blockchain networks. The platform reports over 208 million people and more than $4.4 trillion in cumulative trading volume.

Its services now include perpetual contracts, tokenized stocks, ETFs, yield products, and developer infrastructure. The project is also preparing a dedicated mobile application. Its CAKE ticker and contract address remain unchanged, with existing staking positions unaffected.

Pancake’s relationship with Binance makes this rebrand interesting. Binance Labs unveiled a strategic investment in CAKE in June 2022. The investment supported the decentralized exchange’s development within the BNB Chain ecosystem.

The rivalry becomes clearer when looking beyond the latest announcements. Binance has already introduced its own AI infrastructure through Binance Agent OS. Launched in August 2026, the platform connects compatible AI applications with Binance trading, market data, wallet, and payment capabilities.

It has been revealed that its Model Context Protocol server supports compatible AI agents, including ChatGPT. Developers can build applications that access supported Binance services through user-controlled permissions.

Pancake is also developing its position in this emerging market. In July, the platform partnered with BNB Chain’s Agent Studio to help developers deploy autonomous agents.

These agents can interact with Pancake’s liquidity pools, rebalance positions, and execute trading strategies. Its AI tools also include portfolio planning and assistance across DeFi products.

It has been revealed that this creates an interesting contrast between the two ecosystems. Coinbase is bringing AI-powered trading directly to consumers through ChatGPT. Binance is building infrastructure that allows developers and AI agents to interact with its services. Pancake adds a decentralized execution layer to the wider BNB Chain ecosystem.

In a recent development, the next battle in crypto may not be about which exchange attracts the most human traders. It could be about which infrastructure becomes the preferred destination for AI-powered financial activity.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that when I was a kid, I loved to ride.
  • So when Anyland hit us up to do a review of their fresh Anyland Rev Pro, an all-electric dirt bike capable of 34 mph and assisted wheelies, the inner child in me jumped at the chance.
  • Wheelies look effortless until you try one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that when I was a kid, I loved to ride. Riding a bike, for me, is synonymous with childhood, in fact. We used them to get ourselves places, but we also just used them to entertain ourselves. Inevitably, this led to popping wheelies, building ramps and trying jumps, and doing all sorts of other stuff my Mom just didn’t want to know about, no matter how much I wanted to brag. As an adult, I still love to ride — as the famous saying from Animal Farm goes, “four wheels good, two wheels mo’ bettah!” (I’m paraphrasing, a lot, but you get the point).

So when Anyland hit us up to do a review of their fresh Anyland Rev Pro, an all-electric dirt bike capable of 34 mph and assisted wheelies, the inner child in me jumped at the chance.

Wheelies look effortless until you try one. Anyone who has learned on a dirt bike knows the usual lesson blueprint: too little throttle and the front wheel never lifts, too much and you’re flat on your back. Anyland, a startup electric dirt bike brand, created the Rev Pro as an entry-level electric dirt bike with a controller that lifts the front wheel to a preset angle and holds it there, so a new rider can focus on balance instead of juggling throttle and brake.

The system, which Anyland sells as WELIXON and notes it co-engineered with controller maker Moxin, offers three angle settings: 25°, 35°, and 45°. Riders start at the lowest angle and move up as their balance improves. According to Anyland, the controller delivers continuous, smooth power to keep the front end at the chosen angle, which is designed to reduce the risk of a “loop out,” where the bike flips backward, one of the most common ways wheelie learners get hurt. Once you’re ready, you can switch the assist off, and the Rev Pro behaves like a regular throttle-controlled electric dirt bike for practicing manual wheelies.

In a recent development, underneath the trick, the Rev Pro is a lightweight, mid-drive electric dirt bike. Anyland lists:.

The speed modes set the first speed caps as low as 12 mph, and matter for the audience Anyland is targeting: teenagers and adults who are latest to dirt bikes. Starting in the lowest mode lets a rider build skills before moving up, and gives parents a way to keep a first-timer in a gentler setting.

The Rev Pro arrives in a compact box and includes all the tools you’ll need to set the bike up. My friend and I (two untrained professionals) did it in about 40 minutes:.

According to recent reports, in short, the ride is really fun. I found the suspension incredibly responsive and comfortable, the acceleration smooth and quick, and the riding position much more comfortable than I anticipated. It’s been raining non-stop where I live, so while I got this bike a few weeks ago in the mail, I haven’t had a chance to get it up onto the trails yet, so stay tuned for that. Testing it on the dirt sidewalks and running over curbs demonstrates me it will likely be a great addition to my weekends.

It has been revealed that A wheelie assist doesn’t make any dirt bike risk-free. Wear a helmet, gloves, and protective gear every time, and start in the lowest speed mode at the 25° setting. Practice using the rear brake, supervise younger riders, and stick to private land or designated off-road areas. Check your local rules before riding anywhere else, since many electric dirt bikes aren’t legal on public roads.

Anyland’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday price starts as low as $1,199, and prices have varied, so check the current price before you buy.

It has been revealed that for a startup brand in a crowded field of lookalikes, the Rev Pro’s pitch is simple: a beginner-friendly bike built around one clever feature. If you’ve always wanted to learn a wheelie without the bruises, it’s worth a look.

Thanksgiving Costs at Home Jump 6% in 2026 as Grocery and Utility Bills Hit Hosts Hard

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (719 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, thanksgiving is the perfect time for loved ones to gather over a delicious, hearty meal.
  • According to the American Farm Bureau, the average cost of a 10-person holiday dinner will rise by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person.
  • And unfortunately, the higher price tag doesn’t stop at the grocery store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, thanksgiving is the perfect time for loved ones to gather over a delicious, hearty meal. But in 2026, that feast could come with a higher price tag than we’d like.

According to the American Farm Bureau, the average cost of a 10-person holiday dinner will rise by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person. That’s because staples like turkey, milk, rolls, and cranberries have shot up in price.

And unfortunately, the higher price tag doesn’t stop at the grocery store. You may also notice a spike in your utility bills as your home’s systems are forced to work harder to keep everyone comfortable.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) found that the average family already uses over 300 gallons of water per day at home. With increased usage from additional showers, dishwashing, and hand-washing that are typical during the holidays, costs are sure to climb.

“Having guests over greatly drives up money spent on groceries, but it also drives up utility costs. Preparing all of that food often involves keeping ovens and burners running for multiple hours and using large amounts of water in both the cooking and cleaning processes,” explains Carrie Barnard, founder and recipe developer at Eating on a Dime.

Sources indicate that fortunately, it’s still possible to enjoy Thanksgiving without breaking the bank. A bit of planning and creativity can help keep your grocery expenses and utility bill in check.

Where you live can also impact how much you spend this Thanksgiving.

The American Farm Bureau found that the 10-person classic dinner in the Northeast is about 5% higher than the national average of $61.57.

Costs in the West ($58.74) and Midwest ($56.89) are closer to the national average. And if you live in the South, you could expect to pay around $54.33.

There are a few reasons for these cost differences.

“They largely have to do with supply chains, since different regions require different imports, and these imprints cost more the further they travel,” states Barnard.

Since the Northeast is generally colder, it relies more heavily on imports for many Thanksgiving staples, which leads to a higher cost for consumers. Also, the Northeast typically has higher operating costs for businesses, meaning that grocery prices are often higher.

“However, prices vary widely between different stores, and many of them offer special holiday promotions, so there are usually savings to be found,” Barnard adds.

While grocery and energy costs may be higher this Thanksgiving, these tips can help reduce them and enjoy the holiday without overspending.

Jim Wang, founder at Wallet Hacks in Fulton, MD, suggests exploring promotions at your local supermarkets and groceries.

In a recent development, “Many stores know consumers are being squeezed and often try to put out promos around Thanksgiving. They may offer the turkey at a low cost to get you to make your entire holiday purchase there,” Wang explains.

Depending on how you celebrate Thanksgiving and who attends your meal, a potluck might make sense.

It has been revealed that “Every year, we do a potluck with friends and everyone brings something to share. This defrays the costs across everyone and while you don't end up with nearly as many leftovers, that's also excess spending you can avoid, especially if Thanksgiving leftovers don't excite you,” indicates Wang.

If you’re hosting, be a bit more conservative about how much everyone will eat.

“Sometimes we get concerned about having guests leave hungry and we make too much as a result,” Wang claims.

It’s perfectly OK to make less of the more expensive items, like proteins, and bigger portions of sides that they can fill up on. Chances are your guests may prefer those sides to the turkey anyway.

Barnard tries to use her air fryer and slow cooker rather than my full oven when possible.

“These appliances are highly versatile and able to cook a wide variety of dishes, and they consume much less energy in the process,” explains Barnard.

Unlike ovens, which leak out heat and consume more energy the more you open the door to check on your food, air fryers and slow cookers cook things swiftly and efficiently with low energy.

“I try to only use the oven when it’s required due to the size or amount of food involved,” Barnard adds.

Six new ways to simplify solar installs: Top Rack Technology brings mounting innovation to RE+ 2026

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From smarter waterproofing to 360-degree rail adjustment, Top Rack Technology is putting installer efficiency, rooftop flexibility, and cost control at the center of its latest product lineup.
  • As the solar industry continues to look for ways to reduce installation costs and streamline residential projects, mounting hardware is getting a fresh dose of innovation.
  • Its latest lineup reflects a practical approach to product development: addressing everyday installation challenges while keeping system performance, aesthetics, and affordability in focus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From smarter waterproofing to 360-degree rail adjustment, Top Rack Technology is putting installer efficiency, rooftop flexibility, and cost control at the center of its latest product lineup.

As the solar industry continues to look for ways to reduce installation costs and streamline residential projects, mounting hardware is getting a fresh dose of innovation. Top Rack Technology, Inc. (TRT) is making that case at RE+ 2026, where the solar racking manufacturer is showcasing six new mounting solutions designed to simplify rooftop installations, improve flexibility, and help installers work more efficiently.

Its latest lineup reflects a practical approach to product development: addressing everyday installation challenges while keeping system performance, aesthetics, and affordability in focus.

Six Products, One Common Goal: Better Installation Efficiency.

According to recent reports, among the latest offerings is TRT’s Full-Coverage Skirt System, which targets an crucial consideration in residential solar: appearance. By concealing exposed array edges, the system delivers a cleaner, more finished look that can help installations better complement residential properties.

The latest TRT-G2 Bracket takes aim at installation simplicity and competitive pricing. Designed around practical field requirements, the bracket can be paired with TRT’s ButyLok waterproofing component, creating an integrated attachment and roof-sealing solution.

Sources indicate that waterproofing is particularly key in rooftop solar, where roof penetrations are still a critical consideration for installers and property owners alike. ButyLok introduces a shoe-like component containing pre-applied, gel-like butyl material. When compressed by the G2 bracket, the material spreads across the intended sealing surface, potentially reducing manual sealant application and simplifying the installation process.

It has been revealed that TRT is also introducing SAVRIX, another residential attachment option developed with manufacturing efficiency, installation practicality, and cost competitiveness top of mind.. Meanwhile, the RF-2 Rail Fastener is designed to simplify rail-to-bracket connections.

Top Rack Technology’s FreePivot Bracket features a 360-degree rotatable rail fastener and built-in height adjustment to accommodate varying rooftop conditions and simplify solar panel installations. Credit: Top Rack Technology.

But perhaps the most versatile addition is the FreePivot Bracket. Its 360-degree rotatable rail fastener allows installers to accommodate attachment points that aren’t perfectly aligned. Built-in height adjustment helps compensate for uneven roof surfaces, while its all-metal construction supports durability. The one-orientation design and single-socket installation concept are also intended to reduce tool changes and keep crews moving.

Hardware Meets Digital Project Planning.

Beyond the six new products, TRT is showcasing its established portfolio, including the TRT 01 Rail-less Base System, TRT 02 Rail-Base System, and TRT 03 Tile Hook System.

The company is also highlighting its Online BOM Design Tool, which supports project setup, structural design inputs, module layouts, engineering verification, and automated bill-of-materials generation. Connecting digital planning with physical mounting solutions could offer installers and distributors a more streamlined path from project design to field execution.

Installation hardware doesn’t need to be flashy to make a difference. Improvements in attachment flexibility, waterproofing, assembly time, and aesthetics can translate into meaningful operational advantages.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Regulators approve new agreement to ensure data centers pay for their own energy costs.
  • SALEM, Oregon — The Oregon Public Utility Commission has approved an agreement between advocates and Pacific Power.
  • 1, 2027, upcoming Pacific Power data centers will be held responsible for their own energy costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Regulators approve new agreement to ensure data centers pay for their own energy costs.

SALEM, Oregon — The Oregon Public Utility Commission has approved an agreement between advocates and Pacific Power. Now, Pacific Power customers have a strong suite of protections against data centers’ impact on Oregonians’ energy bills.

Sources indicate that starting Jan. 1, 2027, upcoming Pacific Power data centers will be held responsible for their own energy costs. These new rules will only apply to future data centers and existing ones making significant investments, which regulators identified as the most pressing challenge to address. Right now, the utility has very few existing data centers on its system.

“With a long line of data centers waiting at Pacific Power’s door, I’m confident that we have the right protections at the right time,” remarked Bob Jenks, Executive Director of Oregon Citizens’ Utility Board. “We were able to stop more extreme impacts on power bills just in time.”.

Data centers over 100 MW will also have to pay a small surcharge to fund energy efficiency upgrades for low-income households. This includes funding for deep home retrofits, lowering energy use across the grid while saving customers on monthly bills.

“Many of the households we serve are already struggling to afford their energy bills and risk having their utilities shut off. Data centers will help fund weatherization, energy efficiency upgrades, and the critical home repairs that often prevent our clients from accessing these improvements in the first place,” said Charity Fain, Executive Director of Community Energy Project. “Requiring data centers to cover the costs of the energy infrastructure they need, rather than passing those costs on to residential customers, is an crucial protection for low-income households, seniors, and people with disabilities.”.

Under this order, if there is a power emergency, Pacific Power can prioritize critical energy use for other customers, like renters and homeowners, by curtailing service to data centers. Increased electric demand by data centers strains the grid and increases the potential for blackouts during heat waves or hard freezes.

In a recent development, “This is a massive win that puts Oregon at the forefront of managing data center growth the right way,” said Joshua Basofin, Oregon Clean Energy Program Director at Climate Solutions. “It protects Oregonians from rising costs and strengthens grid resilience. Data centers should not harm our ability to access essential electricity to power our lives and keep us safe all year.”.

It has been revealed that regulators also ruled that upcoming data centers can only be connected to Pacific Power’s grid if there is enough emissions-free electricity available to serve them. Under HB 2021, Pacific Power is required by law to serve all customers with 100% emissions-free electricity by 2040. This new rule will help manage costs for other customers outside of data centers during the transition to clean energy.

“We have long known that clean energy is the most affordable form of energy,” mentioned Ben Brint, Senior Climate Program Director at Oregon Environmental Council. “This ruling is a win for data center accountability, and for Oregonians across the state — especially frontline communities already bearing the brunt of climate impacts and rising energy costs. It will save ratepayers money in the short and long run, allocating costs appropriately while advancing Oregon’s 100% clean energy goals.”.

This change also comes at a time when many Oregonians are calling for broader changes to how the state handles data centers. Impacts on data centers are poised to be an glitch again at the Oregon State Legislature in 2027.

In a recent development, “The POWER Act demonstrated the people’s power to fight back against the rising energy rates and ecosystem harms that large data centers inflict,” said Emily Bowes, Policy Strategist & Acting Director at Sierra Club Oregon. “In 2027, alongside newly introduced and returning climate champions, we will continue to fight for a clean energy transition in Salem and statewide.”.

In a recent development, in 2025, the Oregon Legislature passed the POWER Act to help utilities rein in data centers’ added costs to Oregonians’ energy bills. Last fall, Portland General Electric began the work to roll out this new law in practice. In January, Pacific Power started a similar process for its customers. The next step is to address the few existing data centers on Pacific Power’s system, starting as early as summer 2027. It is unclear if the final phase will include rate adjustments.

Founded in 2016, MegaRobo builds robotic systems that let artificial intelligence software run physical experiments, alongside precision measurement and inspection tools for manufacturers.

Industry observers note that investors joining the round included Oman Investment Authority, Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia, Sinovation Ventures and CMB International. The company raised $600 million to date across multiple funding rounds, including nearly $300 million in Series C during 2022.

Recent findings suggest that “The first generation of AI learned from humanity’s accumulated knowledge. Recent findings suggest that the tech giant’s two most prominently marketed offerings are Megalaxy Lab, an AI-connected experimental platform and CellVue T2000, its automated cell-imaging instrument. Both appear on the company’s English-language homepage. MegaRobo also sells more specialized lab equipment, including the Auflo sample-preparation workstation and the Seloris cell culturing automation system.

The key distinction is that Megalaxy Lab is the public face for the company’s AI-for-science strategy, while CellVue and other systems represent concrete examples of the instruments it builds for the industry.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer said through Megalaxy it is making real-world experimentation programmable and accessible. Researchers and AI agents can configure experiments, route them through automated laboratory systems, track execution, receive structured, machine-readable results, and feed them directly into the next cycle of scientific reasoning. This includes virtual large data readouts that can be amplified as digital twins representing the scientific data, protein design, biochemistry and other properties.

MegaRobo stated it’s working together with industry partners, including Tencent Cloud and Twist Bioscience, to expand its capability in the AI Science community with the launch of Poreva Open, a global AI protein design challenge open to all models and technical approaches. Megalaxy will provide wet-lab validation for more than 10,000 protein design sequences, creating an opportunity to test models against real experimental data.

Sources indicate that the organization is also developing the One Intelligence Stack as a common technology foundation for instruments, machines, materials processes and real-world feedback. It’s not just a collection of isolated AI applications and products, but a chain infrastructure that enables AI to act, learn and observe across complex physical environments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Chris Simms has picked up a $4.5 million New York City residence—after offloading his longtime Connecticut estate for $5.5 million.

The 45-year-old—who retired from the NFL in 2010 following a spleen injury—and his wife, Daniella, recently picked up the property, which is located in Sutton Tower.

His upcoming pad comes complete with three bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms, and floor-to-ceiling windows, according to the New York Post, who first reported the sale. The property also boasts a chef's kitchen and panoramic views.

The Sutton Place tower was built in 2022 by architect Thomas Juul-Hansen. The residence is known to be the tallest tower on the East Side.

As a member of the luxe dwelling, Simms and his wife get access to a resort-style pool, a gym, a personal training studio, saunas, and a spa space.

His purchase came weeks after Realtor.com® exclusively revealed that he sold his Connecticut property for $5.5 million.

He initially put their longtime Greenwich abode on the market on Feb. 6. Within a matter of months, they had dropped the price by $500,000.

A second price cut in June slashed a further $600,000 from the ask, while a third discount on Aug. 21 saw the athlete's original ask of $8 million lowered to $6.2 million, a move that ultimately bagged a buyer for Simms' dwelling.

Simms, who now serves as an analyst for NBC Sports, purchased the home for $2.5 million in 2019—shortly after he and his wife invested heavily in its restoration and renovation.

The property, which was originally built in 1725, has been updated extensively in the seven years since the couple took ownership.

Today, the property is hailed as a "piece of Greenwich history" with all the luxury of a modern mansion.

"A fully restored antique farmhouse offering approximately 3,669 square feet of refined living space, set on extraordinary level acreage with sweeping meadow views and an irreplaceable country setting across from protected conservation land with direct access to the Greenwich Riding Trails," the listing, which was held by Monica Webster of Douglas Elliman, noted.

The five-bedroom, five-bathroom dwelling features an open floor plan that begins with a living area with a cozy fireplace, windows, and wooden beams on the ceiling.

The chef's kitchen boasts state-of-the-art appliances, a white marble island, and white cabinetry.

The charming dining area also has wooden beams on the ceiling and a wooden island.

The bedrooms follow the home's minimalistic aesthetic and feature enough space for a queen-sized bed while boasting small windows.

"The residence blends historic authenticity with modern luxury, featuring wide-plank antique floors, exposed beams, preserved fireplaces, and original architectural details," the listing added.

The bathrooms feature double vanities, a large glass-enclosed shower, a marble soaking tub, and sliding barn doors.

Elsewhere, there is a gym, spa center with a massage chair, and an outdoor entertaining area with a foosball table.

Throughout the home, modern aesthetics have been meticulously merged with historic charm.

"A thoughtful renovation delivers elevated comfort throughout, including a newly created primary suite with cathedral ceilings, floor-to-ceiling windows, a bespoke dressing room, and a private staircase to a serene, light-filled office and library retreat for everyday living," the listing stated.

Simms and his wife lived in Greenwich for many years, having previously sold another dwelling in the area for $2.7 million before relocating to their farmhouse.

They chose the farmhouse for its impressive parcel, noting to the outlet that they wanted more space for their horses.

However, they are now choosing to call to Upcoming York home.

Before settling down in Connecticut, Simms enjoyed a lengthy career in the NFL, a career that began at the University of Texas at Austin, after which he was drafted by the Buccaneers as the last pick of the final round in the 2003 NFL draft.

It has been revealed that simms remained with Tampa Bay until 2008, when he was released by the team. He was later picked up by the Tennessee Titans, with whom he played for a year before moving on to the Denver Broncos.

After a brief return to the Titans, the quarterback's career came to an end, with many pointing to a 2006 spleen injury as the reason for his retirement from the NFL.

He briefly tried his hand at coaching, signing with the Upcoming England Patriots in 2012 as an offensive coach, as well as a scouting expert, but he made a move into broadcasting after just a few months.

Simms and his wife, who met in high school, tied the knot in 2004 and now share two children.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs. Although major drivetrain components often receive the spotlight, one overlooked system can have an outsized impact on turbine reliability and performance: gearbox oil cooling.

Recent findings suggest that heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes. When cooling systems become clogged with airborne debris, dust, or organic material, oil temperatures rise, lubrication performance declines, and component stress increases. Over time, these conditions can contribute to reduced gearbox efficiency, elevated maintenance demands, and avoidable downtime.

It has been revealed that “Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs. Technologies that improve cooling efficiency and reduce service exposure can have a meaningful impact on long-term turbine reliability and operational profitability,” according to Mike Erickson, HYDAC’s Market Manager for the Wind Industry.

It has been revealed that traditional “panel cut” heat exchanger designs have long been susceptible to clogging due to their tightly packed fin structures. In many wind environments — particularly agricultural, dusty, or high-pollen regions — debris accumulation can severely restrict airflow. Oil leaks can further compound the matter by trapping contaminants within the exchanger core, making cleaning more difficult and labor intensive.

This operational challenge has driven the need for more resilient cooling technologies designed specifically for real-world wind farm conditions.

HYDAC’s upcoming “Square Wave” heat exchanger design represents a significant advancement in addressing these reliability concerns. Engineered to allow debris to pass more freely through the exchanger fins, the design minimizes clogging while improving cooling efficiency under demanding operating conditions.

The importance of effective cooling cannot be overstated. Wind turbine gearbox oil typically operates within an optimal temperature range of approximately 45°C to 65°C. Even modest temperature increases can significantly impact oil viscosity. According to field data, a 12°C rise in oil temperature can reduce viscosity by nearly 28 percent — affecting lubrication quality and accelerating wear on critical drivetrain components.

Recent findings suggest that field trials have demonstrated measurable operational benefits from the Square Wave design. During a one-year trial on GE 1.x turbines, the upgraded exchanger consistently reduced clogging and lowered maintenance requirements compared to traditional panel cut cores. Operators reported reduced up-tower cleaning time and fewer temperature-related cooling faults.

Field validation across multiple turbine platforms has further reinforced the operational advantages of the Square Wave design. In one case study involving legacy 1 MW-class turbines operating in the Pacific Northwest, a major renewable energy operator installed pilot sets of Square Wave heat exchangers as part of a cooling performance evaluation. Installation teams reported the upgraded exchangers integrated seamlessly into the existing platform with no retrofit complications.

According to recent reports, after initial operating data demonstrated improved cooling consistency, the operator expanded the evaluation program with additional units. Long-term SCADA analysis later showed turbines equipped with Square Wave technology operate approximately 20 to 25 percent cooler than comparable turbines using conventional heat exchanger designs under similar operating conditions. The data also highlighted another important advantage: the Square Wave cores continued to maintain airflow and cooling efficiency in debris-heavy environments where traditional exchanger designs became increasingly restricted over time.

The successful deployment also generated interest from additional wind service organizations seeking retrofit-ready cooling upgrades that could improve turbine reliability while reducing maintenance burdens across aging fleets.

Sources indicate that “What operators are increasingly recognizing is that small improvements in thermal management can create meaningful gains in turbine reliability, maintenance efficiency, and long-term asset performance,” mentioned Erickson. “The field data we’re seeing continues to validate the value of designing cooling systems specifically for real-world wind operating environments.”.

In a recent development, more recently, long-term SCADA data from Mitsubishi platforms further validated the technology’s performance. After two years of operation, turbines equipped with Square Wave heat exchangers operated approximately 19 to 25 percent cooler than reference turbines using standard exchanger designs under comparable operating conditions.

Sources indicate that for wind asset owners and service providers, the implications are substantial: Improved thermal management supports healthier oil viscosity, more stable gearbox operation, and potentially longer component life. At the same time, reduced cleaning frequency and fewer cooling-related service events translate directly into lower operational expenditures and increased turbine availability.

As the industry continues to prioritize lifecycle optimization and energy production efficiency, innovative subsystem upgrades such as advanced heat exchanger technology are becoming increasingly valuable. Rather than waiting for costly failures or performance degradation, operators are seeking practical retrofit solutions that improve reliability without requiring major system redesigns.

It has been revealed that “Effective thermal management is critical to protecting gearbox health and maintaining oil performance over time. By addressing one of the most common causes of cooling degradation — debris accumulation — operators can improve uptime while reducing unnecessary maintenance interventions,” said HYDAC’s Erickson.

For wind stakeholders evaluating ways to improve gearbox reliability, reduce maintenance exposure, and enhance turbine performance, cooling system optimization deserves greater attention. Proven retrofit technologies like advanced heat exchanger designs can offer a practical path toward improved uptime and operational efficiency without requiring major system overhauls.

In a recent development, as fleets age and performance expectations continue to rise, collaboration between operators, service providers, and technology partners will be essential to building more resilient wind assets for the future. Now is the time to evaluate whether existing cooling systems are supporting — or limiting — long-term turbine reliability goals.

It has been revealed that “HYDAC’s goal is to help wind owners and service providers solve practical operational challenges in ways that create long-term value across the entire asset lifecycle. Innovations like the Square Wave heat exchanger are designed to improve reliability, simplify maintenance, and support greater energy production over time.”.

Don’t let cooling system limitations impact turbine performance.

  • The milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC.
  • In a recent development, “Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” noted Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that OLMEDO, Spain, Nov. 19, 2026 — AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) today revealed that Project Olmedo, the solar installation at the center of its first Virtual Power Purchase Agreement (VPPA), has completed construction and commissioning and is expected to begin delivering renewable electricity to the Spanish power grid in the coming months, pending final regulatory approvals. BRUC, one of the largest renewable energy groups in Spain, built the new solar installation in the northwest province of Valladolid.

The milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC. The installation’s two solar projects, Los Silos and El Granero, span approximately 300 hectares (741 acres) and hold approximately 150,000 solar panels. AGCO’s portion of the installation’s annual production is expected to be approximately 150 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of renewable electricity a year, equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of approximately 40,000 European households, based on Eurostat data.

In a recent development, “Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” noted Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer. “In volatile energy markets, securing that stability for 10 years strengthens the resilience of our supply chain while supporting upcoming renewable generation.”.

A VPPA lets a company support new renewable energy projects without taking direct delivery of the electricity they generate. Because AGCO’s agreement supported the construction of a brand-new installation, it will add new renewable capacity to the grid rather than drawing on existing sources, a principle known as additionality. The agreement also helps reduce AGCO’s Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased electricity in its Europe/Middle East (EME) region and supports its commitment to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 55% by 2033 from a 2022 baseline.

Industry observers note that “Additionality is what makes this agreement truly meaningful,” said Roger Batkin, Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary. “We did not simply buy renewable electricity that already existed; we supported the construction of a brand-new renewable solar project. Accomplishing this project required over two years of involvement from many teams, functions, and areas of expertise across AGCO, along with technical advisory support from Schneider Electric and a strong partnership with BRUC.”.

Reflecting AGCO’s Farmer-First strategy, Project Olmedo supports local farmers to further diversify their land use by leasing land for the project while maintaining the option for livestock to graze among the panels, maintaining the vegetation in place of machinery.

Sources indicate that AGCO and BRUC leaders, joined by local community representatives José Emilio Escudero García, Mayor of Bocigas, and Ursino Vara Pérez, Mayor of Almenara de Adaja, marked the milestone with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the site in November. Additional drone footage from Project Olmedo and the ribbon-cutting event are available on AGCO’s YouTube page.

For more details on AGCO’s sustainability initiatives, visit the company’s sustainability webpage and read the 2025 Sustainability Report. For more information about BRUC, visit the company’s website at brucenergy.com.

According to recent reports, AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) is a global leader in agricultural machinery and precision agriculture technologies. Driven by a Farmer-First strategy, AGCO delivers value through its differentiated leading brands, Fendt™, Massey Ferguson™, PTx™ and Valtra™. AGCO’s high-performance equipment and smart farming solutions, including brand-agnostic retrofit technologies and autonomous offerings, empower farmers to drive productivity while sustainably feeding the world. For more information, visit www.agcocorp.com.

#99413. 7 6.2-Liter V8s Ranked From Least To Most Horsepower

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1582 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

7 6.2-Liter V8s Ranked From Least To Most Horsepower

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 6.2-liter V8 holds a special place in the hearts of modern muscle-car fans.
  • True, some V8-powered supercars can top the horsepower output from these 6.2-liter units.
  • Engine displacement is generally displayed in cubic liters today, but many automakers do their measuring in terms of cubic centimeters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 6.2-liter V8 holds a special place in the hearts of modern muscle-car fans. After all, a motor that size was under the hood of the dearly departed third-generation Dodge Challenger — in which it indicated off a horsepower rating well into four-figure territory — and Dodge isn't the only automaker to use a beefy 6.2-liter V8.

True, some V8-powered supercars can top the horsepower output from these 6.2-liter units. The Hennessey Venom F5, for one, touts 1,817 horses from its 6.6-liter twin-turbo V8. But 6.2-liter V8s, whether they're naturally aspirated, turbocharged, or supercharged, are among some of the most powerful and most well-liked powerplants of all time. We'll get into the details below, but there are all sorts of rides like the Ford F-150 Raptor, the first mid-engine Chevrolet Corvette, the Chevy Camaro ZL-1, and various Mercedes-Benz AMG models ranging from the C 63 to the SLS AMG that use impressive 6.2-liter V8s.

We do have a disclaimer, though. Engine displacement is generally displayed in cubic liters today, but many automakers do their measuring in terms of cubic centimeters. Then they round up to get to liters. For instance, Dodge's 6.2-liter Hemi V8 actually displaces closer to 6,166 cubic centimeters, so the numbers aren't hyper-precise, but we figure it's close enough.

The trail-ready Ford F-150 SVT Raptor hit dealerships in 2010 with an optional 6.2-liter unit capped at 400 hp. Ford then made that engine standard, with 411 ponies, the following year. Known by Blue Oval fans and insiders as "the Boss" – though it was unrelated to the V8s of the Boss Mustangs — it could propel the Raptor from zero to 60 mph in 6.6 seconds.

Recent findings suggest that ford started the engine's development with a goal of producing a so-called Triple Seven – a 7.0-liter V8 capable of 700 hp with a redline of 7,000 rpm. The single example made, many years later, would find its way into a 2005 Ford Mustang dragster that could get through the quarter mile in under 9 seconds. Who knows what kind of numbers the Raptor would have put up if Ford's 7.0-liter ended up under the hood? Even without it, though, the massive-power pickup truck was an impressive rig.

For a certain subset of AMG enthusiasts, this is where it all started. The naturally aspirated 6.2-liter M156 V8 was the first motor ever developed from scratch by MB's in-house performance division. All previous AMG vehicles had relied on modified Mercedes-Benz production engines. Of course, many of those engines were built by hand. The Mercedes-AMG philosophy of "one man, one engine" goes back to at least 1976, when the firm had relocated to Affalterbach, Germany.

As for the first car with the M156, that distinction goes to the 2007 Mercedes-AMG E63, which won Car and Driver's German Sports Sedan Comparo that same year. No doubt impacting the decision, the naturally aspirated engine kicked out a healthy 507 hp and 446 pound-feet of torque. When C&D put that output to the test, the car rolled out to 60 in a mere 4.2 seconds, dispatching the quarter mile in 12.6 seconds at 115 mph. By 2010, the E63's M156 came with 518 hp complemented by 465 lb-ft of torque.

The M156 would end up motivating the likes of the R230 SL 63 AMG, the CLK 63, CL 63, CLS 63, and ML 63, but it's notable to note that the "63" attached to these machines was a bit of a misnomer. The M156's displacement remained at 6.2 liters in all these applications.

Industry observers note that the M159 started out with healthy horsepower, and it increased in output over the years. When the car premiered in 2010, its engine could make 563 horsepower, and the AMG SLS GT could serve up 583 horses from 2013-2015.

It has been revealed that the 6.2-liter V8 powering the 2020 Mercedes-AMG SLS Black Series made 622 horsepower, which might seem meager by modern supercar standards, but that power output comes from a naturally aspirated mill. What's more, this engine wasn't simply an updated version of the M156 6.2-liter V8. The significant updates ranged from dry-sump lubrication to redesigned camshafts to the kind of lightweight forged pistons needed by some high-performance rides. In all, some 120 of the M159's components were upgraded compared to the M156.

It's further worth pointing out that Mercedes refers to the engine as having 6.3 liters of displacement. You can chalk that up to marketing, however. To honor Mercedes' first post-war V8, the 6.3-liter M100, the company decided to also call the M156 a 6.3-liter mill — despite it displacing 6,208 cubic centimeters. That, obviously, should be rounded down to 6.2. Anyways, the naming strategy then carried over to the M159.

Industry observers note that as Chevy's high-performance halo car, it makes sense that the Corvette — especially in its ZR1 variants — has been the showcase for some of the brand's most powerful engines. So we're going to talk about two different versions of the Corvette's 6.2-liter V8: the LT5 from the 2019 ZR1, and the LS9 that came in the 2009 ZR1. First, it's the LS9.

Putting out a stout 638 horsepower, the LS9 is part of GM's long-running LS lineup, which is considered a totally different engine generation than the LT roster. One core practical difference is that the former featured port injection and the latter had direct injection, cylinder deactivation, and variable valve timing. Drilling down into the details demonstrates the LS and LT families are set apart by much more than that — there's practically zero parts interchangeability between the two.

It has been revealed that the LS9 proved its performance credibility on the road with zero-to-60 sprints of 3.4 seconds and a top speed of 205 mph. When it debuted, it was Chevy's most powerful production motor.

In a recent development, when Chevrolet ended production of the front-engine Corvette, it sent the car out on top: The 2019 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 debuted as the fastest, most powerful model to ever wear the Crossed Flags badge. Yes, both benchmarks have since been obliterated by the record-setting Corvette ZR1X, but the '19 ZR1 was no slouch. During testing at Car and Driver, the ZR1 covered the quarter mile in 10.7 seconds, reaching 135 mph along the way, and along the way it went from zero to 60 in 2.9 seconds.

Industry observers note that the engine backing those results was Chevy's supercharged 6.2-liter LT5 V8. Now, GM has a tendency to re-use its engine codes, so keep in mind that this is a totally different mill from the 5.7-liter LT5 V8 that Lotus developed for the 1990 ZR-1.

It has been revealed that oh, and the hand-built 2019 LT5 also set a record itself. The LT5's 755 hp and 715 lb-ft represented the most output ever offered in any production Chevy up to that point. Another milestone — the premiere of GM's first dual fuel-injection system — was a key contributor to the output. With that on board, the LT5 had both direct and port injection working for it.

Before it was adapted to be fueled by ethanol and got a huge horsepower bump as a result, the "regular" Demon spent time as the most powerful muscle car in the world. Despite its street-legal status, the Demon was purpose-built for the dragstrip. There, it could make the most of its supercharged 6.2-liter V8 and enter the record books. The Demon tapped into 840 hp to cover the quarter mile in 9.65 seconds at 140 mph, making it the fastest production car in the quarter mile at the time.

The Demon was plenty different from its Hellcat predecessor. To be more specific, while it was technically the same engine, the Demon's V8 shared fewer than 40% of its components with the standard Hellcat. Notable enhancements here extended to a reinforced block with upgraded main caps and deck surfaces, along with a forged alloy crankshaft, forged pistons, and powder-forged connecting rods. Compared to the Demon's 840 hp, the standard Hellcat's 707 hp output seems almost pedestrian.

In a recent development, dodge first debuted a supercharged 6.2-liter Hemi V8 for the 2015 Challenger SRT Hellcat, setting a template for the increasingly insane Dodge V8s that followed. The basic progression was from the Hellcat to the aforementioned Demon, and eventually to the Demon 170, with each set of changes major enough to count as a different engine.

Consider the 2023 Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170. The most powerful muscle car in the world when it released — according to Dodge – this street-legal stunner can spit out 1,250 hp and 945 lb-ft when drinking E85 ethanol fuel. On E10, it still offers up a hefty 900 horses. And although its supercharged 6.2-liter V8 shares its displacement with its predecessors, that's about all it shares. With the exception of the camshaft, just about every internal component on the Demon 170 was changed.

For one thing, to maximize its fluid intake, fresh fuel injectors capable of delivering more than 2.7 gallons of fuel per minute were used. On the air side of the fuel-air mixture, the 3.0-liter supercharger benefited from enhancements to its throttle body, pulley, intake valves, valve guides, bearings, connecting rods, and more. The outcome was a machine that could sprint to 60 in an EV-like 1.66 seconds on a race-prepped surface — just as fast as the Rimac Nevera R that set 24 new performance records in 2025.

#99412. The Ultimate Playbook To Buying a Home Without 20% Down Using Grants and Assistance Programs

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1940 w)

The Ultimate Playbook To Buying a Home Without 20% Down Using Grants and Assistance Programs

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.
  • Industry observers note that many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home.
  • Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.

Industry observers note that many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home. But that's not necessarily true.

Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.

Sources indicate that these programs can help buyers snag a home by providing cash that can go toward a down payment. There are even loan programs for certain qualified buyers that don't require any down payments. The array of offerings from federal, local, and private sources can take the form of looser loan requirements, outright grants of money, or tax credits, all of which make homeownership more affordable.

First-time homebuyers, often with certain qualifications, are often beneficiaries of the assistance. Lower-income buyers, those who serve in the military or are veterans, and those who purchase fixer-uppers or homes in rural areas might also be eligible for the help.

The assistance ranges greatly, from a grant of several thousand dollars to, at the high end, a savings of five figures over the life of the loan.

Down payment assistance can take several forms and can even help buyers circumvent the PMI payment.

Recent findings suggest that while 20% down has been something of a gold standard for homebuyers, it's also the minimum that generally lets them avoid private mortgage insurance, or PMI, which is assessed because lenders believe the loan carries risk. This in turn raises the homebuyer’s monthly expenses.

It has been revealed that here's an example: PMI is typically 0.5% to 1% of the loan amount per year. So if buyers put down less than 20% and their mortgage is $300,000, their PMI would be between $1,500 and $3,000 per year. That would add about $125 to $250 per month on top of their mortgage payment, a significant charge. (Homeowners can have PMI canceled when the equity in their home surpasses 20%.).

So, while a buyer can also choose loans that require a down payment of just a single digit, that PMI can stretch a budget paper-thin. That's where down payment assistance can help.

Industry observers note that at least 2,000 such programs exist across the country. Some are federal, but most tend to be at state and local levels, which is important to know when searching for help. Private organizations, from lenders to nonprofits, also work with borrowers who need help.

It has been revealed that these programs might offer grants, loans, tax credits, or a combination of a couple of these benefits. Funding can come from our government, nonprofits, and private enterprises. Let’s take a closer look:.

Grants might be the most desirable form of down payment assistance. Typically, a grant is fully forgiven at closing and never has to be paid back. Yes, we’re talking about free money!

About 7% of down payment help comes in the form of grants, indicates Veronica Khandelwal, vice president of HFA Relations at Down Payment Resource, which provides consumers with guidance on this kind of assistance. But there is a catch.

“Grants require owner occupancy," she claims of the requirement for buyers to live in these properties. That's to make sure these loans don't go to investors or vacation-home buyers. "Some programs allow grants to be applied to multifamily purchases of one to four units so long as one of the units is occupied by the borrower.".

Forgivable loans are another option. These loans need to be repaid only if a repayment trigger event occurs, such as the home being sold before the end of the term, the home being no longer owner-occupied, the title being transferred, or the loan being defaulted on.

Deferred-payment loans are also available. These are paid back either at the end of the loan term or if a repayment trigger occurs. So, while it’s not a gift, it will help homebuyers get over that down payment hurdle and buy a house they might otherwise not have been able to afford.

According to recent reports, repayable loans are another leg up on homeownership. They require borrowers to make monthly payments, like a typical loan. But here's the good part: They do so at interest rates starting as low as 0%. That helps spread the down payment and closing costs over a number of years, making it much easier to enter the housing market.

Some agencies also offer a combination of these forms of assistance. That could mean that a portion of the help will be forgiven (or “written off” with no repayment needed), while some will need to be repaid. Tax credits are sometimes offered as well, further sweetening the deal.

Each down payment assistance program will have its own rules and guidelines, but the vast majority are offered only for a home that buyers will live in as a primary residence.

Here are some of the more popular national options folks might access to help them to pivot from home shopper to homebuyer.

FHA (Federal Housing Authority) loans were created by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for first-time homeowners (HUD). These mortgages allow as little as 3.5% for the down payment, provided buyers have a credit score of 580 or higher, along with other qualifying factors. The federal government insures these loans, and for that reason, banks are more willing to loan money to homebuyers who have neither top-tier credit nor loads of cash to put down on the purchase.

Sources indicate that FHA Section 203(k) loans require only 3% down, provided qualifying buyers will live in the property, typically one that needs work, while they fix it up. For buyers hoping for a DIY route into a dream home, this could be a win-win. The cost of improvements is included in the loan so buyers can finance both the home and up to $35,000 in repairs.

But buyers beware: The cost of materials and construction labor has spiked since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and work is taking much longer to be completed than ever before.

According to recent reports, VA (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs) loans might be offered directly by the VA or backed by the department. Several factors are considered, such as service history, duty status, income, and credit rating. But those who qualify can purchase a home with zero down as long as the sales price isn’t higher than the home’s appraised value.

In a recent development, fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are federally funded loans that can help buyers skirt steep down payments. The Home Possible, HomeReady, and HomeOne loans typically offer a 3% down payment mortgage to qualifying, lower-income homebuyers.

Industry observers note that good Neighbor Next Door is another HUD-sponsored program. In this case, law enforcement officers, teachers, firefighters, and emergency medical technicians can enjoy a substantial incentive in the form of a discount of 50% from the list price of the home in a community that is being revitalized. The buyer must live in the house for three years as a primary residence.

Sources indicate that teacher Next Door Grant is a program similar to the one above but is designed to help educators own their own homes. Grants to the tune of up to $8,000 in certain areas are possible with additional down payment assistance available in some circumstances.

The USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) Rural Home Loan Program was created to assist people buying homes in rural locations. For qualifying, single-family properties, loans might be available with no money down. There are maximum income limits and other qualifications to be eligible for one of these mortgages.

There are plenty of other programs available as well. Different states and cities, as well as individual lenders and nonprofits, can help prospective homebuyers get the financing they need. Folks should put their location and "down payment assistance" into a search engine, and take a look at what's available. They might see everything from Habitat for Humanity to local religious organizations pop up. Also,visit Down Payment Resource.

It has been revealed that one other path to explore is whether a buyer's job provides down payment assistance. A lot of employers may offer assistance in  the form of a $10,000 loan that is forgivable after five years.

In a recent development, down payments hit a four-year low at the start of 2026. The median payment fell to $23,400 and 12.8% in Q1 2026, down 19% and 1.2 ppts year over year.

However, down payments remain well above pre-pandemic levels, as more buying is happening in the lower-down-payment South and Midwest, even as the Northeast stays deeply competitive.

It has been revealed that the Northeast posted the highest median down payment at $57,600, reflecting higher home prices and more competition. The Northeast also sees the largest gap between what buyers are paying as a down payment today compared to pre-pandemic.

Compared to 2019, the Northeast has seen down payments climb 236.8%, significantly more than the next closest gap of 134.0% in the Midwest. These trends are consistent with the persistent upward pressure on home prices in these regions as scarce inventory is met with sustained buyer demand.

Get ready for some good news. There are a lot of misconceptions about who qualifies for down payment assistance.

Industry observers note that “Many people think these programs are only available to low-income borrowers, first-time homebuyers, or for properties that have sales price limits,” says Down Payment Resource's Khandelwal. “But if you look, you’ll find specialized programs designed to assist specific groups, including first-generation homebuyers, minorities, Indigenous people, people of color, veterans, those with government jobs, disabilities, and more.”.

Here’s something else to smile about: A first-time homebuyer doesn't just mean someone who's never bought a home before.

In a recent development, the federal government generally holds a broader definition of a first-time homebuyer. It’s someone who has not been a homeowner in the past three years. If you sold a house three-and-a-half years ago, you qualify as first-time buyer.

Buyers can take several different steps to find a down payment assistance program that’s right for them.

Check the federal programs mentioned above (like HUD, VA, USDA, Fannie Mae, and Freddie Mac), and see if there’s anything suitable.

According to recent reports, buyers should also visit their state’s Department of Housing website and see what might be listed, or call their number and inquire what down payment assistance programs might be available. Cities, towns, private lenders, and nonprofits may also have help.

“Homebuyers should seek the assistance of a mortgage lender who specializes in affordable lending to identify their best options,” advises Khandelwal.

In terms of what is typically needed to access aid, the documentation is very much in line with what’s needed to apply for any mortgage. Buyers will likely need the following:.

Pay stubs plus W-2s from the past few years to verify employment and income history.

Any 1099 forms showing other income.

Details on the property they intend to buy (The real estate agent can share this information.).

The paperwork is processed in much the same way as a home loan, and there may be requests for more documents.

Then, if buyers are approved, they will be ready to move ahead with a lower—or no—down payment as their homeownership journey unfolds.

#99411. 2026 Genesis GV80 Coupe Is An Appeal To Your Heart, Not Your Head

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1323 w)

2026 Genesis GV80 Coupe Is An Appeal To Your Heart, Not Your Head

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1323 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like just about everything Genesis makes, the GV80 Coupe is a fabulous-looking vehicle, perhaps the best-looking in its class with its distinctive front end, lovely silhouette and ducktail spoiler out back.
  • Sure, it runs on low-profile all-season rubber, has seat bolsters that hug you in corners, and is powered by a twin-turbocharged and electronically supercharged 3.5-liter V6.
  • Full Disclosure: Genesis was kind enough to lend me a 2026 GV80 Coupe with a full tank of fuel to do with as I pleased for a week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like just about everything Genesis makes, the GV80 Coupe is a fabulous-looking vehicle, perhaps the best-looking in its class with its distinctive front end, lovely silhouette and ducktail spoiler out back. And like most crossover coupes, the GV80 Coupe promises to lean more into the sporty side of things than its normal-backed brother. The thing is, it doesn't quite deliver on that.

Sure, it runs on low-profile all-season rubber, has seat bolsters that hug you in corners, and is powered by a twin-turbocharged and electronically supercharged 3.5-liter V6. It even has bright red seatbelts, but the GV80 Coupe is by no means a sports car. Hell, it's barely sporty and is certainly lacking a bit in the body control area when compared to stuff like the BMW X6 and Mercedes-Benz GLE Coupe. However, if you take the idea of sporty pretentions out of your head, you're in for a much better time, because the GV80 Coupe is a wonderful, delightfully comfortable cruiser with a well-thought-out interior, lots of top-notch luxury gizmos, and practicality that punches far above what you'd expect from a crossover coupe.

Full Disclosure: Genesis was kind enough to lend me a 2026 GV80 Coupe with a full tank of fuel to do with as I pleased for a week.

It has been revealed that there are two engine options for the GV80 Coupe. A twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6 that pumps out 375 horsepower comes as standard, but those who aren't lilbabybois can step up to the more powerful (and certainly more interesting) twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6 that has a 48-volt system with an electric supercharger. This funky motor throws down 409 hp and 405 lb-ft of torque while also getting slightly better gas mileage than the standard motor. Don't worry, it's still not good fuel economy. The EPA rates it at 17 mpg city, 22 mpg highway and 19 mpg combined. It's a thirsty beast, but that's a small price to pay for all of this modest sportiness.

Granted, the GV80 E-SC, fitted with a Genesis-built 8-speed automatic that sends power to all four wheels, can get a move on in a straight line. It'll hit 60 mph from a standstill in 5.2 seconds, according to Car and Driver's testing, which is solid for a 5,132-pound crossover. The GV80 doesn't feel like it's in much of a rush to accelerate, though, and it also lags behind its competition. Without a doubt, it's a smooth powertrain, but it's not exactly sporty — not in the way the red seatbelts would imply.

Recent findings suggest that the lack of sportiness becomes incredibly obvious when hustling the GV80 Coupe around a corner. It's almost as if those seatbelts are red not to denote sportiness, but to show how miffed the car is that I dare push it. The lack of athleticism is evident almost immediately, as the suspension and brakes have a tough time keeping up with the beefy curb weight. There's just too much body roll and not enough steering feel to make for any sort of fun-spirited driving no matter what drive mode I was in, including the E-Supercharged-exclusive Sport+ mode.

What I learned quickly is that this car really shines as a cruiser. I've said in the past that crossover coupes are the personal luxury coupes of the modern age, and that's true again with the GV80 Coupe. This thing is wonderfully comfortable to eat highway miles in or blast around town as the Ergo Motion driver's seat works on that knot in my back and HMG's wonderful suite of driver-assistance aids keep me in my lane and out of the rear bumper of the car in front of me. The engine, while interesting in its operation, doesn't provide the most inspiring noise, so it's not the end of the world when it shuts up as I drive in quiet, calm luxury through the streets of Upcoming York.

Industry observers note that beyond those lovely quilted leather seats, the interior of the GV80 Coupe is a fantastic place to be that also goes toward its cruising pretensions. Sure, there's some carbon-fiber-look trim, but it doesn't exactly scream sportiness. Neither does the wood, metal, glass, and swaths of suede. Do ya know what that does scream? Nice. Pleasant. Chill. Good.

Industry observers note that another nice, pleasant, chill, and good element of the GV80's interior is its 27-inch OLED touchscreen that serves as both a digital gauge cluster and center infotainment display. Inputs can be made with either fingers or an iDrive-style control knob. I'll admit, the system feels a bit clunky to use the first day or so, a step behind BMW and Mercedes-Benz's new systems, but after a bit of learning where everything else is, it becomes second nature. Using wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto fixes that problem quickly, too. Adding to the simplicity is the secondary touchscreen below it that has all of the car's climate controls housed within it, and between the two screens is a row of buttons that can pull up core vehicle controls. It's certainly welcome for the Luddites among us.

Recent findings suggest that aside from the sloping roofline, not too much else was changed on the inside or outside for the Coupe, which isn't a bad thing as the GV80 is a lovely-looking vehicle from the get-go. The GV80 Coupe carries the same 116.3-inch wheelbase as the regular GV80, but overall length increases by an inch to 195.5 inches, and the rakish roofline drops overall height by 0.2 inches. Rear seat occupants probably aren't going to miss the 0.8 inches of headroom they've given up, and if they are ones to complain, ditch them. You don't need that sort of negativity in your life, anyway. You're going to need to trim the fat regardless, because there's no third row in the Coupe.

Recent findings suggest that the GV80 Coupe is no exception when it comes to crossover coupes being a bit silly. No truly practical person would buy one over the normal crossover they're based on simply because they're an exercise in style over substance. They're innately compromised products, and on top of that, they almost always cost more.

In a recent development, A base-base GV80 2.5T RWD starts at $59,195 including destination, but that's not really a fair comparison, so let's look at the GV80 3.5T Advanced AWD — that's the trim level where the Coupe starts from. The regular GV80 in that spec starts at $77,445, while a comparable GV80 Coupe is going to be $83,345. That means you, dear buyer, need to fork over an extra $5,900 for the pleasure of having fewer seats and worse visibility out the rear. I, however, would contend that that is a small price to pay for such a pretty car. Argue with a wall.

Recent findings suggest that the GV80 I drove was no base-spec, though, as it had the E-Supercharger, boosting its starting price to $89,145. The vehicle's lone option, $650 worth of Bering Blue Paint, brought the final price to $89,795. It's a small price to pay for something that looks this good — it's nearly a concept car for the road, if you ask me. If you think of the GV80 Coupe as a piece of art rather than a car, then it's a hell of a deal, and it's even fairly in line with alternatives from Germany like the Mercedes-Benz GLE450 Coupe ($82,650), Audi Q8 Premium ($78,295), BMW X6 40i xDrive ($78,750) and Porsche Cayenne Coupe ($97,450). It's worth the premium over the latter four based on looks alone.

Of course, if you look at it compared to the normal GV80, things fall apart, but this is a car meant to speak to your heart, not your head. Just take a second to look at the mess your head's gotten you into throughout your life. Perhaps it's time to let your heart make some decisions.

Hitachi Vantara bets smarter storage can close AI’s pilot-to-production gap

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that enterprises pushing AI from pilot to production are learning that data, not GPUs, is the hardest part, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg are part of the answer.
  • That pressure is turning storage into an active layer that classifies, governs and serves data to models.
  • In a recent development, “Storage is not seen as just storing the data,” Raman remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 13:39 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Industry observers note that enterprises pushing AI from pilot to production are learning that data, not GPUs, is the hardest part, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg are part of the answer. Demand for AI infrastructure reveals few signs of slowing, but much of the information companies need is still scattered, ungoverned and out of reach.

That pressure is turning storage into an active layer that classifies, governs and serves data to models. Unstructured files such as logs and medical images hold intelligence AI can now extract, according to Arun Prasad Raman (pictured, left), vice president of hybrid cloud and AI infrastructure at Hitachi Vantara Corp.

In a recent development, “Storage is not seen as just storing the data,” Raman remarked. “You need to bring in more intelligence natively rather than moving the data to another replication and bringing it back for, say, indexing. If it can do it natively, that’s where the value add is.”.

Industry observers note that raman and Jeff Lundberg (right), principal product and solutions manager at Hitachi Vantara, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI’s pilot-to-production gap, Apache Iceberg and how Hitachi Vantara is adding intelligence to storage. (* Disclosure below.).

Reference architectures for AI factories and data platforms are largely settled. Most projects stall because data is spread across on-premises systems, software-as-a-service applications and the cloud, while access control, governance and shifting regulations add friction, according to Lundberg. Hitachi Vantara is responding with industry-specific solutions built on its Hitachi iQ stack and its sister businesses’ rail and energy experience, he explained.

Sources indicate that “It’s about the outcome more so than the technology that we’re trying to put into place,” Lundberg mentioned. “That’s an enabler to get you to the solution you’re trying to get to.”.

Much of that work now happens in storage. Last week, Hitachi Vantara expanded its VSP One platform with new object storage and data lakehouse capabilities. A service in its object store flags files containing personal information, such as Social Security numbers. Data scientists can then keep that data out of specific models or block its replication to another country, Raman explained.

Industry observers note that “That’s the intelligence we are adding into the storage itself,” Raman said. “So that’s where the evolution of storage is making it more intelligent.”.

Analytics follow the same logic. CT scan metadata can be stored in Apache Iceberg format on the company’s object store and queried directly. An application could list every abdominal scan from the past year without a separate extract, transform and load or ETL process or database, Raman noted.

Recent findings suggest that “Whether it’s a backup or it’s 10 years old, it still carries some intelligence,” Raman remarked. “As long as it carries intelligence, it becomes important to AI.”.

In a recent development, washington, DC — Today, the Senate passed the “Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026” following little debate and an insufficient amendment process. BAAJA will now go to the House of Representatives for consideration.

In response, Sierra Club Executive Director Loren Blackford released the following statement:.

“While a rogue president is waging a war on clean energy, the Senate rushed a deeply flawed bill that furthers the buildout of fossil fuels, strips away power from communities and Tribes, threatens our clean water and public lands, and endangers wildlife. They must reject the Senate’s fast-tracked bill and demand debate and consideration to deliver for the people, not corporate polluters and Donald Trump. The American people made a clear call merely weeks ago: our elected leaders must address soaring costs and a corrupt system that prioritizes corporate polluter profits over our health, our wallets, and our future.

According to recent reports, “The Sierra Club thanks the Senators, Tribes, and advocates across the country who raised their voices in the fight to fix this bill. Americans deserve a better deal.”.
